Building and Running

The examples are in the examples folder and are built with the library by CMake:

cmake -S . -B cmake-build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build cmake-build -j
cmake-build/examples/db_infohog          # Linux
cmake-build\examples\Release\db_infohog  # Windows

The database examples pause for Enter between steps; give them empty input (< /dev/null or < nul) to run straight through. The TLS servers need a certificate and key; see Certificates for making test ones. tests/run_tests.sh builds everything and runs the examples against each other and against mock mail and FTPS servers.

Object database

examples/database/simple/testprog.cpp

db_simple: gxDatabase basics: create a file, allocate, write, read and delete blocks, file statistics.

examples/database/database/testprog.cpp

db_database: Store and find fixed-size objects in a gxDatabase file.

examples/database/btree/testprog.cpp

db_btree: gxBtree index with a custom key class: insert, find, walk in order, delete.

examples/database/btree_cached/testprog.cpp

db_btree_cached: The same B-tree operations through a BtreeCache.

examples/database/btree_node/testprog.cpp

db_btree_node: Inside a B-tree node: key layout and branches.

examples/database/database_cache/testprog.cpp

db_database_cache: gxDatabaseCache write-back cache over a database file.

examples/database/defrag/testprog.cpp

db_defrag: Free-space reuse and rebuilding (defragmenting) a database file.

examples/database/pod/testprog.cpp

db_pod: POD: a data file with one or several index files opened together.

examples/database/infohog/infohog.cpp

db_infohog: InfoHog object database: records with a key and variable members, add, find, change, delete, list and reopen.

Object database patterns

examples/oodb/typed_objects.cpp

typed_objects: A typed class sent over gxStream, stored in a gxDatabase, exported to plain text and imported back.

examples/oodb/journal_recovery.cpp

journal_recovery: gxdJournal transactions: a writer killed mid-transaction, Recover(), a consistency check and Rollback(). POSIX only.

examples/oodb/day_events.cpp

day_events: One database file per YYYY/MM/DD folder and a time-range query across days.

examples/oodb/vector_basics.cpp

vector_basics: The vector index: float32, float16 and int8 files, exact against graph search (recall), the l2/cosine/ip metrics, tags and filters, update, delete, repair, a rolled back transaction and the format fields.

examples/oodb/vector_records.cpp

vector_records: Records that carry their own vectors (vector members): record and node in one transaction, records read back by address, Verify() with a resolver, the index rebuilt from the records alone.

examples/oodb/vector_days.cpp

vector_days: One vector index per day searched as one through a .vixset manifest: threads, a day range that skips files, an archived day, a live writer attached.

examples/oodb/vector_search_service.cpp

vector_search_service: Vector searches through the database object server (VECTOR_INFO, VECTOR_SEARCH) over mutual TLS, with a day range. Linux and Windows.

examples/oodb/object_replication.cpp

object_replication: gxObjRepl: a primary and a copy, a few commits read back on the copy, then a planned switch (takeover and rejoin) and more commits, with the digests equal on both nodes. Windows and Linux.

examples/oodb/replication_copy.cpp

replication_copy: A database folder copied with robocopy or cp while its writer is stopped, checked with digests, and the copy's indexes rebuilt from its records after a fault. Windows and Linux.

TLS networking

examples/tls/tls_echo_server.cpp

tls_echo_server: TLS server using gxsTLSServer and a ThreadPool. Usage: tls_echo_server port cert.pem key.pem

examples/tls/tls_echo_client.cpp

tls_echo_client: TLS client with certificate checking. Usage: tls_echo_client host port [--ca ca.pem] [--insecure]

examples/tls/https_get.cpp

https_get: Fetch a URL or download a file with gxsHTTPClient. Usage: https_get url [file] [--ca ca.pem]

examples/tls/https_server.cpp

https_server: Small HTTPS file server built on gxsHTTPReadRequest() and gxsHTTPWriteResponse().

examples/tls/https_check.cpp

https_check: Check a list of web sites over TLS: status, time (fastest/median/slowest with --count), size, redirects, and the response headers with --headers (7.4). Usage: https_check [--head] [--headers] [--count N] [--list file] [--ca ca.pem] url ...

examples/tls/smtp_send.cpp

smtp_send: Send mail over implicit TLS or STARTTLS.

examples/tls/pop3_list.cpp

pop3_list: List and read a POP3 mailbox over TLS.

examples/tls/imap_fetch.cpp

imap_fetch: Read an IMAP mailbox over TLS (or STARTTLS, or plain text for a local server): search, list newest first, save each message once to a spool folder (7.4).

examples/tls/ftps_client.cpp

ftps_client: List, download and upload with FTPS.

examples/tls/dir_upload.cpp

dir_upload: gxsFTPClient: watch a folder and upload each settled file by FTPS (as NAME.part, renamed, size-checked), then delete it or move it to a done folder. The password comes from DR_FTP_PASSWORD or a mode-600 file, never the command line. Usage: dir_upload --dir DIR --host HOST [--port N] --user USER [--password-file FILE] [--ca FILE] [--implicit] [--remote-dir DIR] [--pattern GLOB] [--settle S] [--interval S] [--done DIR] [--once] [--log FILE]

examples/tls/stream_server.cpp

stream_server: gxStream server that stores client blocks in a gxDatabase file.

examples/tls/stream_client.cpp

stream_client: gxStream client that stores and reads back blocks over TLS.

General support

examples/general/config_file.cpp

config_file: gxConfig: write, read and change a configuration file.

examples/general/logfile.cpp

logfile: LogFile shared by several threads.

examples/general/thread_pool.cpp

thread_pool: ThreadPool tasks, results and exceptions.

examples/general/trading_sessions.cpp

trading_sessions: CDate and systime.h: US market sessions, holidays, trading days.

examples/general/string_utils.cpp

string_utils: strutil.h, base 64 and CRC-32, each checked against a known answer.

examples/general/service_example.cpp

service_example: gxProcessLock and the frame of a long-running program: one instance, work every few seconds, a clean stop on SIGTERM, Ctrl+C, a stop file or the Windows service manager; --daemon on POSIX, --install/--service/--uninstall on Windows (demand start, LocalService). Exit 2 if another instance runs. Usage: service_example [--name NAME] --lock FILE --log FILE [--stop-file FILE] [--interval S] [--run-for S] [--daemon]; service_example --service ... (started by the service manager); service_example --install ... / --uninstall [--name NAME] (as administrator).

examples/general/csv_merge.cpp

csv_merge: gxCSVReader and gxCSVWriter: merge two spreadsheets exported as CSV on a key column. Usage: csv_merge [--inner] [--delimiter C] KEY A.csv B.csv [OUT.csv]

Plain text diagnostics

examples/diagnostics/ping.cpp

ping: ICMP and ICMPv6 echo. Usage: ping host [count] [-4|-6]

examples/diagnostics/telnet_client.cpp

telnet_client: Telnet login and command (plain text; trusted networks only).

examples/diagnostics/serial_read.cpp

serial_read: gxSerialComm: read a serial port (Linux /dev/ttyS0, /dev/ttyUSB0 or a pty; Windows COM1...) to standard output or a capture file flushed after every read. Usage: serial_read DEVICE [--baud N] [--parity N|E|O] [--bits 7|8] [--stop 1|2] [--flow none|hard|soft] [--out FILE] [--hex] [--seconds N] [--bytes N] [--quiet]. Windows: COM10 and up are opened as \\.\COMn, reads end within 100 ms (the time limit and Ctrl+C are seen at once), standard output is binary; a serial line has no hangup there, so the read runs to Ctrl+C, --seconds or --bytes.

examples/diagnostics/udp_broadcast.cpp

udp_broadcast: Send and receive UDP broadcast datagrams with gxSocket (plain text; trusted local networks only) (7.4).

examples/diagnostics/udp_multicast.cpp

udp_multicast: Send and receive IPv4 or IPv6 multicast datagrams, join a group (plain text; trusted local networks only) (7.4).
